answer.evidence: The main body is a tall, flat blue panel (rows 6-29) with white Korean glyphs. It is a vertical face seen straight on, with a constant width of 13 and no receding top. The head (rows 1-4, width 9 to 11, then 13) is a small cap with highlight rows at 1 and 3. It has a darker line at row 4 and a dark row at row 5, but it reads as a thin front-facing cap or lip of about 2 usable rows, not a foreshortened horizontal surface. There is no ellipse, roof or visible contents. The base is a 1-row light strip at row 30 and the outline is at row 31. Overall this is a front elevation, like the wrong reference examples with a rim-only top.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a narrow vertical sign with a dark navy body, a lighter edge highlight and white Korean lettering. It shows 7 visible tones per tile, 0% near-flat coverage and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so its outline is tinted navy rather than black. That matches bus-shelter-a (6 tones) but is well below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). The body is mostly a dark blue ramp of about 4 steps, with little grain or per-pixel texture beyond the lettering and the edge highlight. Next to the kiosk and vending machine it reads somewhat thinner and flatter, though it is a simple sign and not a sticker-style piece. Tile density sits at the low end of the references and is not clearly equal to them.

surfaces.part: sign panel with Korean text (front face)

answer.evidence: This is a tall sign with a 13px-wide body. At the top, rows 1-3 form a lighter blue cap band (#5e80b2 and #3d578a) with white highlight pixels. Row 4 is a darker line (#2d436e) and row 5 is a near-black line (#091125) acting as eave shadow. The silhouette steps out from 9 to 11 to 13 px over rows 0-3, so the cap is slightly rounded or tapered. The cap is about 4 rows and reads as a small top surface with a front-edge line, though it is a marginal case. Below it, rows 6-29 are a flat, front-facing panel with white Korean glyphs, and row 30 is a grey base strip. The front face is about 25 rows, with no receding side face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tall, narrow navy sign with white Korean lettering and a lighter edge highlight. It measures 7 visible tones per tile, 0% near-flat coverage and 0% neutral dark edge pixels. That matches bus-shelter-a (6 tones, 9% flat) and is above it on flatness, but below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). The outline is a dark navy that leans toward the body colour, not neutral black, so it reads as a dark material tone. The body has about 4 steps (highlight edge, mid blue, dark blue, deep outline) and the text adds contrast. It has no grain, speckle or panel detail, so the blue body is a fairly smooth fill, with less detail than the kiosk and vending references. It is a thin, sparse object, so I do not fail it on density alone. Next to the references it still looks a little simpler and flatter. It is acceptable but not clearly equal, and when in doubt the rule is to fail.

surfaces.part: sign panel with Korean text (front face)

answer.evidence: The sign is a tall vertical panel. Rows 6-30 are a flat south face carrying the text, with a dark outline and a light base strip at rows 30-31. At the top, rows 1-3 form a lighter blue cap that is narrower than the body (11 px against 13 px). It ends in a darker front-edge line at row 4 and a dark shadow or outline at row 5, which reads as a small top surface sitting on the panel. The cap is only about 4 rows, so this is a weak top, but it does have an edge line and shadow rather than being just a 1-2 row rim. The face below is well over 3 rows, so the object is not a flat slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin vertical sign, so I judged density by eye as well as by the numbers. It has about 5 navy steps: a dark blue-tinted outline, a mid body, a lighter edge highlight, a shaded side and the white lettering. The measured facts are 7 visible tones per tile, 0% near-flat coverage and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline leans blue and is not a black sticker line. This matches bus-shelter-a (6 tones, 9% flat) and sits below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20), which are much busier objects. The body is not a flat fill, since the edge highlight and shading break it up, and the lettering adds detail. It is a little simpler than the richer references but would not look thinner or flatter than bus-shelter-a beside them.

A dark row 5 follows as eave shadow above the panel face, so the cap reads as a small top surface. It is thin and marginal. The base strip at row 30 is only a 1-row lip.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tall navy vertical sign with white Korean glyphs.
